newsitem.title: USA: BP Alaska chief Morgan to retire.
newsitem.headline: BP Alaska chief Morgan to retire.

text.p: John Morgan, president of British Petroleum unit BP Exploration (Alaska) Inc., will retire at the end of January, the company said Monday.
Morgan, who has been with BP for more than 30 years and has headed the Alaska unit since January 1994, will return to Britain, the company said.

"This decision is a personal one on my part," Morgan said in a company statement. "After a most enjoyable career with BP, it's time to move on to a new phase of life and work. It will be with considerable sadness that we say good-bye to our many friends in Alaska."

His successor will be Richard Campbell, a senior manager for BP in Colombia, the company said. Campbell has worked in Colombia for five years, has 27 years' experience in oil and gas exploration and production, and will assume his Alaska duties on Jan. 1, BP said.

While in Alaska, Morgan served on the Governor's Oil and Gas Policy Commission, a panel established by Gov. Tony Knowles to consider ways to stimulate the state's oil industry. Before he came to Alaska, Morgan was general manager of BP's North Sea activities.
